title: Mughal Architecture

cards.b: Mughal architecture is a staple of Prelims. The question is usually who built what, material, and features. Track the path from red sandstone (Akbar) to white marble (Shah Jahan).

Babur built mosques at Panipat (Kabuli Bagh) and Sambhal and gardens (charbagh). Humayun’s Tomb, Delhi (1565–72, built by Haji Begum, Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas): first garden-tomb, red sandstone with white marble; double dome; UNESCO site 1993. Sher Shah built the Qila-i-Kuhna and his tomb at Sasaram, an octagonal tomb on a lake.

Red sandstone, fusion with Hindu and Gujarati styles. Agra Fort; Fatehpur Sikri (1571–85): Buland Darwaza (1576, victory over Gujarat), Jama Masjid, Diwan-i-Khas, Panch Mahal, Jodha Bai’s palace, Salim Chishti’s tomb in white marble; Akbar’s tomb at Sikandra (Agra). Fatehpur Sikri was abandoned due to water shortage.

Itimad-ud-Daulah’s tomb (Agra, 1622–28, by Nur Jahan): first Mughal building entirely in white marble with pietra dura inlay (parchin kari); sometimes called the “baby Taj”. Gardens: Shalimar Bagh and Nishat Bagh, Kashmir. Jahangir’s tomb at Lahore.

The golden age of Mughal architecture: Taj Mahal (1632–53, Ustad Ahmad Lahori; double dome, minarets, four-part charbagh; UNESCO 1983), Red Fort and Jama Masjid in Delhi, Moti Masjid in Agra, Diwan-i-Aam and Khas (“If there is a paradise on earth…”), Shalimar Bagh Lahore, Peacock Throne. The city Shahjahanabad (1648).

Badshahi Mosque (Lahore, 1673), Moti Masjid in the Red Fort, and Bibi ka Maqbara (Aurangabad), a weak copy of the Taj built by his son Azam Shah. Royal patronage declined, but regional Mughal styles flowered in Awadh (Bara Imambara, Lucknow) and the Deccan.

Features are Persian (charbagh, iwan, double dome, pietra dura) but craftsmen and motifs are Indian (chhatris, jharokhas, brackets, lotus). Percy Brown called it a synthesis. Gardens symbolised paradise; the Taj plan shows the river-side garden, unlike the usual tomb at the centre.

The Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri, Humayun’s Tomb and Red Fort are UNESCO sites. Taj Trapezium Zone rules limit pollution near the Taj (M. C. Mehta case, 1996). The Red Fort hosts the Independence Day speech; it was taken up under the “Adopt a Heritage” scheme (2017).

• “Trace evolution of Mughal architecture.”
